A1.justification: The title, authors, research problem and algorithms match. Both PDFs are readable through their final appendices, and their equations and algorithm displays support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, sample-complexity theorems and proofs, but no original empirical outcomes in the main text or Appendices A–E.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and Appendices A–G. Its added two-state lower-bound construction is a mathematical argument, not an experiment or simulation.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the capped Geom(0.5) MLMC estimator and the same two-stage, anchored TD updates for value and average-reward estimation. The newly constructed semi-norm changes the analysis, not the algorithmic procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical datasets or evaluation tasks. Contamination, TV and Wasserstein uncertainty remain the theoretical setting; the added two-state lower-bound example is not evaluated experimentally.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed algorithms. References to prior robust RL and MLMC methods remain literature discussion.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to norms in convergence guarantees are mathematical revisions, not changes to experimental metrics or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, empirical robustness tests or case studies. The added assumption analysis and lower-bound construction are formal theoretical developments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The analytical treatment of estimator bias and variance does not introduce empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains observed performance values, rankings or qualitative empirical findings. Revisions to analytical bounds and their constants are covered under T1.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the span-contraction argument with constructed semi-norms and substantially new proofs in Section 3 and Appendix C. It adds small-radius conditions ensuring ergodicity in Appendix B, quotient-norm constructions in Appendix D, norm-equivalence constants and revised convergence bounds in Appendix F, and a two-state optimality argument in F.2. Lemma 2 also removes the TV bound's factor (1 + 1/delta), although its retained proof in Eq. (107) still contains that factor.

C1.justification: A central advertised contribution changes from contraction under the span semi-norm to contraction under a specially constructed semi-norm, throughout the abstract, contribution list and conclusion. The abstract also replaces 'finite constant' sampling complexity with 'finite expected' complexity. The first finite-sample analysis and epsilon^-2 complexity claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains why multistep mixing does not itself provide one-step span contraction and discusses when nominal-kernel ergodicity suffices for small uncertainty radii. Its conclusion newly identifies the ergodicity requirement and scaling through function approximation as limitations.

D1.justification: The sampling parameter, truncation rule, anchoring procedure and step-size prescriptions remain. Neither version supplies code access, hardware information or empirical reproduction settings; the added norm constructions are theoretical proofs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Berger and Wang (1992), Horn and Johnson (2012), Wirth (2002), and Chen et al. (2025) for the revised mathematical foundations, while removing Gupta et al. (2015), Norris (1998), and Puterman (1994). The positioning relative to prior robust average-reward and discounted RL remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Appendix A, and the main biased stochastic-approximation section moves into Appendix D. v2 condenses the formulation, reorganizes the Bellman-operator material, introduces main-text proof sketches, and revises headings and explanatory passages. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: Both retain the single-column format and the same two algorithm displays, with no figures or data tables. v2 makes the pseudocode more compact by shortening inputs and conditions, combines some displayed equations, and relocates displays with the reorganized sections.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful explanations, applicability conditions and limitations, and replaces v1's unsupported inference from multistep to one-step span contraction. However, the replacement proof relies on identifying individual spectral-radius bounds with uniform matrix-product decay in Appendix C.2, while Lemma 8's quotient-norm calculation drops a remaining term from Eq. (64). These unresolved steps underpin the retained convergence claims, so the clearer presentation does not establish a reliable net improvement in this theory paper.
